Mail arrives from the whole internet, including a lot of spam, and must land in the right inbox. People open, search, send and attach. Never lose a message, and keep search fast even over years of mail.
Audience: 2 million people; normal peak ≈ 9000 requests/s; budget ≈ $30000/month.
Concepts: Search is a copy, Hot, warm, cold and archive, Waiting instead of breaking, Designs that other teams must live with, Inside a storage engine.

### Notes that sync across your devices
https://systemdesigner.io/p/device-notes/
Hard; Productivity.
Build a notebook that works on a phone and laptop, including a month offline. Edits should reach connected foreground devices in under a second, concurrent work must not disappear, and the server should not need plaintext notes. Push wakes devices; durable sync must work when push does not.
Audience: 1 million people with about 3 devices each (approx.); normal peak ≈ 3000 requests/s; budget ≈ $4400/month.
Concepts: Syncing across devices, Ordering and time, Privacy by design, What consistent really means, Work across services.

### Shopping cart
https://systemdesigner.io/p/shopping-cart/
Easy; Commerce and retail.
Shoppers browse products, drop things in a cart and come back later from another phone. Browsing is most of the traffic and can be a little old. The cart itself must always show what the shopper just added.
Audience: 10 million shoppers a month (approx.); normal peak ≈ 3000 requests/s; budget ≈ $4200/month.
Concepts: Remembering answers, Which copy is the truth.

### Flash sale inventory
https://systemdesigner.io/p/flash-sale-inventory/
Medium; Commerce and retail.
At noon a hot item goes on sale with only a few thousand units. A huge crowd arrives in the same minute and everyone taps Buy. Stock must never go below zero, nobody should be charged for an item that is gone, and the site must not fall over.
Audience: 4 million shoppers on the day (approx.); normal peak ≈ 2500 requests/s; budget ≈ $13000/month.
Concepts: When one item is popular, Waiting instead of breaking.

### Black Friday marketplace
https://systemdesigner.io/p/black-friday-marketplace/
Hard; Commerce and retail.
Once a year a marketplace puts thousands of deals live at the same minute. Millions browse and search, a few doorbuster items get hammered, and a smaller crowd checks out. A payment must never be taken twice, and the day must survive the card processor having a bad hour.
Audience: 30 million shoppers on the day (approx.); normal peak ≈ 20000 requests/s; budget ≈ $44000/month.
Concepts: Remembering answers, When one item is popular, Exactly once, on purpose, Many customers on one system, Work across services, Changing a running system.

### One-time code by text
https://systemdesigner.io/p/otp-sms-delivery/
Easy; Telecom and messaging.
Apps ask you to send a six-digit code to a phone. The code must arrive in seconds, a person must never get it twice, and nobody may use your system to spam a number. Texts go through a carrier partner with a hard speed limit and a real price per message.
Audience: 3 million people a month (approx.); normal peak ≈ 40 requests/s; budget ≈ $94000/month.
Concepts: Exactly once, on purpose, Saying "slow down" politely.

### Voice and video call setup
https://systemdesigner.io/p/call-routing/
Medium; Telecom and messaging.
People tap a name and expect the other phone to ring in a second or two. Your job is the setup: find where the person is, ring their devices and connect the two sides. Everyone calls at the same moments, like evenings and holidays.
Audience: 40 million people a month (approx.); normal peak ≈ 15000 requests/s; budget ≈ $29000/month.
Concepts: Live sockets and presence, Surviving a region.

### Bulk text campaigns
https://systemdesigner.io/p/bulk-sms-campaigns/
Hard; Telecom and messaging.
Businesses send a coupon or an alert to hundreds of thousands of phones at once. Carriers accept texts only at a fixed speed, every text costs real money, and a person who replied STOP must never be texted again. Delivery receipts come back by the thousand and must be counted.
Audience: 60 thousand businesses (approx.); normal peak ≈ 30 requests/s; budget ≈ $140000/month.
Concepts: Waiting instead of breaking, Saying "slow down" politely, Exactly once, on purpose.

### Status page
https://systemdesigner.io/p/status-page/
Easy; Developer platforms.
When a big service has a problem, millions of people open its status page to see what is happening. The page must stay up exactly when everything else is down, and it must not share a home with the thing it reports on. A few staff update it by hand.
Audience: 5 million visitors in a bad week (approx.); normal peak ≈ 800 requests/s; budget ≈ $3500/month.
Concepts: Surviving a region, Copies near users, SLOs and error budgets, The simplest thing that works.

### CI/CD build system
https://systemdesigner.io/p/ci-cd-pipeline/
Medium; Developer platforms.
Every time a developer saves code to the shared repository, you build and test it. Thousands of developers do this all day, and release day brings a rush. Builds must start quickly, but idle build machines cost real money.
Audience: 40,000 developers; normal peak ≈ 300 requests/s; budget ≈ $106000/month.
Concepts: Waiting instead of breaking, Where the money goes, Adding servers, and why it is late, Changing a running system, Designs that other teams must live with.

### Feature flag service
https://systemdesigner.io/p/feature-flag-service/
Medium; Developer platforms.
Companies turn features on and off for groups of users without redeploying. Millions of apps ask "is this on for me?", and the answer must be instant. A wrong flag value can take down an entire customer, so changes must roll out safely and be reversible in seconds.
Audience: 2,000 customer companies, 5 million app instances; normal peak ≈ 25000 requests/s; budget ≈ $54000/month.
Concepts: Live sockets and presence, Copies near users, What consistent really means, Changing a running system.

### Clickstream analytics
https://systemdesigner.io/p/clickstream-analytics/
Medium; Developer platforms.
Every tap and page view on a busy site sends a tiny event to you. Hundreds of millions pile up each day. Analysts open dashboards to ask what happened this hour. Never drop an event, and keep the storage bill under control as the pile grows.
Audience: Events from 30 million visitors a month (approx.); normal peak ≈ 8000 requests/s; budget ≈ $72000/month.
Concepts: Waiting instead of breaking, Hot, warm, cold and archive.

### Metrics platform
https://systemdesigner.io/p/observability-platform/
Hard; Developer platforms.
Thousands of services send a stream of measurements: CPU, errors, latency. You store them, draw the dashboards and fire the alerts. The platform watching everyone else must never go down first, and one customer creating millions of new series can ruin the bill.
Audience: 2,000 services and their on-call teams; normal peak ≈ 14000 requests/s; budget ≈ $77000/month.
Concepts: Splitting data, Seeing problems early, Surviving a region, How metrics systems work, Many customers on one system, Logs and traces, SLOs and error budgets.

### Logs platform
https://systemdesigner.io/p/logs-platform/
Hard; Developer platforms.
Build a shared log service for 2,000 teams. Collectors send compressed chunks, and on-call engineers find logs by tenant, service and time before filtering their words. A wide search or a runaway label must not stop other teams from investigating an outage.
Audience: 2,000 tenant teams (approx.); normal peak ≈ 100 requests/s; budget ≈ $8800/month.
Concepts: Logs and traces, Consistent hashing and moving data, Inside a storage engine, Many customers on one system, SLOs and error budgets.

### Tracing platform
https://systemdesigner.io/p/tracing-platform/
Hard; Developer platforms.
Store distributed traces for 500 teams and make an exemplar link open the useful trace during an incident. Decide what to sample before storage, handle late spans, and keep query traffic from overwhelming ingestion. Keeping all errors is a policy goal with a failure boundary, not a magic property of sampling.
Audience: 500 teams and their services (approx.); normal peak ≈ 100 requests/s; budget ≈ $2400/month.
Concepts: Logs and traces, Ordering and time, Consistent hashing and moving data, Inside a storage engine, SLOs and error budgets.

### Metrics for many customers
https://systemdesigner.io/p/tenant-metrics/
Hard; Developer platforms.
Build one metrics platform for 5,000 customers. A tenant can create millions of series or run a costly month-long query by mistake. Your design must preserve useful ingestion and query service for the other tenants, and show the offending customer a clear limit rather than an unexplained gap.
Audience: 5,000 tenant organizations (approx.); normal peak ≈ 8000 requests/s; budget ≈ $19000/month.
Concepts: How metrics systems work, Many customers on one system, Copies and quorums, Consistent hashing and moving data, SLOs and error budgets.

## Lesson catalogue

### Your first system
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/intro/
Start; 3 minutes. Build a tiny app in three minutes and keep it standing through a rush of visitors.
Key point: A system is a few boxes in a line, and design is deciding which boxes and how many. Count first: the first practice problem, a URL shortener at about 5,000 requests a second, needs about 6 servers, not 3 (approx.).

### What a request is, and p50 versus p99
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/requests-and-latency/
Start; 3 minutes. A request is one question and one answer. Averages hide the slow ones that people remember.
Key point: Judge a system by its slow requests, and remember distance is part of latency.

### Numbers you can do in your head
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/back-of-envelope/
Start; 3 minutes. Turn monthly users into requests per second and servers needed, with a pencil.
Key point: Divide by 100,000 for a day, multiply by 3 for the peak, and leave headroom.

### Spreading load
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/load-balancing/
Scale the front; 3 minutes. A load balancer hands each request to a free server so none is overwhelmed.
Key point: A load balancer lets many servers act as one, and hides the ones that fail.

### Remembering answers
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/caching/
Scale the front; 3 minutes. A cache keeps recent answers in memory so the database is asked less.
Key point: A cache trades a little freshness for a lot of speed and a calmer database.

### Copies near users
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/cdn/
Scale the front; 3 minutes. A CDN keeps copies of files and pages close to people, so your servers see far fewer requests.
Key point: Put copies of shared content near people; keep your servers for what only they can do.

### Adding servers, and why it is late
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/autoscaling/
Scale the front; 3 minutes. Autoscaling adds servers when busy, but new servers take minutes to start.
Key point: Autoscaling follows the crowd; for known surges, scale ahead of it.

### Copies are a little behind
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/replication-lag/
Scale the data; 3 minutes. Read copies share the load, but they trail the original by a moment.
Key point: Replicas scale reads. Asynchronous replicas can lag behind the primary; synchronous replication waits for the required acknowledgements before confirming a write, trading latency for stronger guarantees.

### Splitting data
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/sharding/
Scale the data; 3 minutes. When one database cannot take the writes, split the data across several.
Key point: Shard when writes or size outgrow one machine, and pick a key that spreads evenly.

### When one item is popular
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/hot-keys/
Scale the data; 3 minutes. Sharding spreads keys, not popularity. One star item can still overload one shard.
Key point: Spread keys with shards and spread attention with caches and copies.

### Search is a copy
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/search-indexing/
Scale the data; 3 minutes. A search index is a second copy of your data, shaped for finding words fast.
Key point: Keep one source of truth and feed purpose-built copies for search.

### Hot, warm, cold and archive
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/storage-tiers/
Scale the data; 3 minutes. Old data is rarely read, so keep it somewhere cheaper and slower.
Key point: Match storage to how often data is read, and move it down as it ages.

### Waiting instead of breaking
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/queues-backpressure/
Work later; 3 minutes. A queue lets a burst wait in line instead of crashing the thing behind it.
Key point: Queues turn spikes into waiting; backpressure stops the waiting from growing forever.

### One post, millions of feeds
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/fanout/
Work later; 3 minutes. A post by a celebrity must reach millions of feeds; do it in the background.
Key point: Do heavy fan-out in the background, and treat huge accounts differently.

### Live sockets and presence
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/realtime-connections/
Work later; 3 minutes. Chat and live scores keep a connection open; that changes how you count capacity.
Key point: Count open connections, not just requests, and keep presence light.

### Which copy is the truth
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/consistency/
Stay correct; 3 minutes. With several copies, you choose between always-latest and always-fast.
Key point: Pick the strongest guarantee only where being wrong would hurt.

### Exactly once, on purpose
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/idempotency-retries/
Stay correct; 3 minutes. Retries are normal, so every action must be safe to repeat.
Key point: Give every action a key, and repeating it becomes harmless.

### Saying "slow down" politely
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/rate-limiting/
Stay up; 3 minutes. A limit per client stops one noisy caller or a flood from taking everyone down.
Key point: Limit each caller so one flood cannot become everyone's outage.

### Timeouts and failing fast
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/circuit-breakers/
Stay up; 3 minutes. When a dependency is slow, give up early so your servers do not pile up waiting.
Key point: Wait briefly, stop calling what is failing, and have a fallback.

### Surviving a region
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/multi-region/
Stay up; 4 minutes. A whole region can go dark. Run in two, and send people to the one that is up.
Key point: Multiple regions buy survival at the price of cost and harder data.

### Seeing problems early
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/observability/
Stay up; 3 minutes. You cannot fix what you cannot see: metrics, alerts and a way back.
Key point: Watch what users feel, tell a human fast, and keep a way back.

### Where the money goes
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/cost/
Business; 3 minutes. Every box has a monthly price. Good design meets the goal without waste.
Key point: Meet the goal with the least you can; money is a requirement too.

### Proof built in
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/security-compliance/
Business; 3 minutes. Auditors want proof: who did what, who can see what, and that data is protected.
Key point: Build the proof in from the start; adding it after the audit is far harder.

### GPUs, tokens and fallbacks
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/ai-serving/
Business; 3 minutes. Serving AI answers is slow and expensive, so cache, limit, and have a fallback.
Key point: Cache, cap and fall back; GPUs are the scarcest part of the system.

### Consistent hashing and moving data
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/consistent-hashing/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Adding one machine can mean moving a little data or nearly all of it.
Key point: Plan the ownership change and the bytes it moves, not just the final node count.

### Copies and quorums
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/copies-quorums/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Copies tolerate failures when placement, acknowledgements and repair match the promise.
Key point: Name the replica set, acknowledgement count, failure model and reconciliation rule together.

### Agreeing on one leader
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/leader-consensus/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. A leader needs a safe election and a way to stop old owners from acting.
Key point: Consensus preserves one committed order; fencing carries that authority to the resource.

### What consistent really means
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/consistency-models/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Choose the guarantee for each operation and name what a partition changes.
Key point: Ask which operation, which order and which failure, then choose the smallest sufficient guarantee.

### Inside a storage engine
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/storage-engine/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. The path from a write to disk decides memory, I/O and cost.
Key point: Size the physical reads, writes and memory under background work, not just the incoming payload.

### Work across services
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/work-across-services/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Make each step durable and show the user what is still pending.
Key point: Commit locally, publish through an outbox, and make every later effect safe to repeat or reconcile.

### Ordering and time
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/ordering-time/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. A timestamp can sort events without proving which event caused another.
Key point: Use clocks to express what is known, and choose an explicit policy for concurrent work.

### Syncing across devices
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/device-sync/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Offline edits need durable local intent, a cursor and a plan for old devices.
Key point: Save intent locally, resume with stable ids and cursors, and keep enough history to merge safely.

### Privacy by design
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/privacy-design/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. The safest data to protect is data the service never receives.
Key point: Choose what leaves the device, who holds keys and how deletion finishes before collecting data.

### How metrics systems work
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/metrics-systems/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Series count, replication and query work decide the size of a metrics platform.
Key point: Budget series, samples, replicated bytes and scanned query work separately.

### Logs and traces
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/logs-traces/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Keep enough evidence to explain failures without indexing or retaining everything.
Key point: Choose the index and sampling policy from the questions people need to answer.

### SLOs and error budgets
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/slos-error-budgets/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Turn a user promise into a budget and an actionable alert.
Key point: Choose a measurable user promise, then page when its budget is being spent fast enough to need action.

### Many customers on one system
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/multi-tenancy/
Go deeper; 7 minutes. Fairness and failure boundaries matter as much as total capacity.
Key point: Limit work per tenant and trace every shared dependency before claiming a small blast radius.

### How to lead a design interview
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/lead-interview/
Lead the design; 6 minutes. Use the hour to make decisions, test assumptions and invite useful disagreement.
Key point: Lead with a user promise, make assumptions testable and spend depth where it can change the design.

### The simplest thing that works
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/simplest-design/
Lead the design; 7 minutes. Include people, failure recovery and future triggers in the cost of a design.
Key point: Choose the smallest design that meets the promise, and attach measured triggers to future complexity.

### Changing a running system
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/running-migrations/
Lead the design; 7 minutes. A safe migration preserves compatibility through the whole rollback window.
Key point: Migrate through compatible states and prove that rollback still understands the data.

### Designs that other teams must live with
https://systemdesigner.io/learn/team-boundaries/
Lead the design; 7 minutes. A boundary is a contract and an operating responsibility, not just a box.
Key point: Name the invariant, the owner and the compatibility promise before drawing a team boundary.
